title: Batcher and Kernel Sampling Playbook: Runtime Benchmarking & Regression Journal
content:
Purpose:
This playbook outlines a repeatable microbenchmarking harness and a sampling strategy for kernel and batcher-level traces to catch regressions in the serving runtime. It focuses on KV cache behavior, batching scheduler interactions, and kernel selection side-effects (quantized vs fp16 paths). The goal is to make perf regressions reproducible and actionable so rollbacks/mitigations can be quickly executed.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target workloads: interactive chat (low token-per-request, latency-sensitive) and batch generation (high throughput, long sequences).
- Hardware: A100 80GB, H100, and a quantization-targeted T4-like profile for edge testing. Harness must be portable across these.
- Models: Llama-family (multi-size), MPT-30B, and a smaller 7B reference.
- The harness should remain environment-agnostic (CI GPUs vs dedicated perf cluster) and support deterministic seeds and synthetic prompt distributions.

Key definitions:
- Microbench: short, focused tests measuring single-op latency (single-token generate with warmed KV).
- Trace sample: a captured request-level span that includes batcher decisions, kernel selection metadata, kv-cache hits/misses and per-kernel runtime.
- Regression guard: automated check that compares current run to baseline and flags behavior outside thresholds.

Design overview:
1) Workload families
   - Interaction (low-batch): 1–8 concurrent connections, seq in [16..256], P95 latency target per token.
   - Mixed (tail heavy): mixture with 80% short (<=64), 20% long (>=1024).
   - Bulk throughput: large batch sizes, continuous generation with pipeline parallelism stress.

2) Harness components
   - Orchestrator: a lightweight runner that schedules trials (env setup, model variant, quantization flag, sequence lengths, concurrency) and emits structured CSV/JSON metrics.
   - Injected probe: small shim inserted in the runtime to emit microtraces at important lifecycle points: batcher enqueue, batch formation, kernel dispatch, kv-cache lookup/eviction.
   - Trace sampler: probabilistic sampler (configurable) that writes proto-like flattened traces to the harness artifact store. Default 0.5% for production-like cluster runs, 100% in perf cluster runs.
   - Baseline store: canonical baseline JSON bundles per-model-per-hardware that the regression guard compares against.

3) Trace format (flattened string fields to keep storage simple)
   Fields we capture per sampled request:
   - run_id, trial_id, model, hw_variant, quant_mode, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, concurrency, batch_size_formed, batch_timeout_ms, kernel_variant, kernel_ms, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_lookups, kv_cache_evictions, kvcache_warm_start, host_cpu_ms, gpu_queue_ms, total_request_ms, timestamp

Bench recipes (canonical microbench jobs):
- Single-token warmed: 1000 sequential single-token generations with KV prepopulated. Emphasis: kernel warm vs cold, KV hit rate should be ~100%.
- Cold-kv-walk: make 250 requests with maximal random prompts so kvcache misses dominate; measure miss penalties and eviction churn.
- Batcher-scaling sweep: vary offered concurrency from 1 to 256 and measure throughput/latency and batch size distribution. This exposes unfair scheduling or starvation.
- Kernel-path A/B: run identical workload with quant_mode set to fp16 and int8/quantized kernels to measure kernel selection delta.

Regression detection heuristics:
- Latency (p95) regression: alert if p95 increased by >= 10% and absolute increase >= 3ms for latency-sensitive trials.
- Throughput regression: throttle if steady-state throughput drops by >= 8% on bulk trials.
- KV cache integrity: if kv_cache_hits / kv_cache_lookups decreases by > 5 percentage points or evictions per minute increase by > 50% vs baseline.
- Kernel deviation: if average kernel_ms for a kernel_variant increases > 15%, mark as kernel-performance regression.
- Statistical validation: use bootstrap resampling with 1k iterations to ensure noise is not being flagged; only surface if p < 0.05 after adjustment.

Instrumentation notes (how traces are produced):
- Lightweight event pairs (enqueue/dequeue) are annotated with batch_id, batch_size, offered_time, dispatch_time. Kernel dispatch includes kernel_variant (string), lib_version and nvcc-like flags.
- KV cache API surfaces: lookup(key_id) returns (hit:bool, age_ms). Instrumentation increments counters exposed via /metrics and emits sample fields.
- Use a microtrace header injected into request context (trace-sample-id) so the generated logs can be correlated with APM traces (Honeycomb/OTel).

Storage and artifacts:
- Each trial emits two artifacts: metrics.csv (tabular aggregated metrics) and traces.ndjson (one flattened trace per line). Filename pattern: model_hw_quant_trialid_{date}.
- Attach both artifacts to JIRA regression tickets automatically and to the GitHub PR that caused the run (if applicable).

Operational playbook for a flagged regression:
1) Triage: determine scope (single model, all models, single hw). Compare traces.ndjson to baseline and look for:
   - Elevated host_cpu_ms before dispatch (scheduling storm).
   - Increase in kv_cache_miss latency (indicates eviction/locking).
   - Kernel_ms spike correlated with a new lib/kernel change.
2) If kernel-related: revert PR for kernel selection heuristic or restrict heuristic to experimental flag.
3) If batcher scheduling: roll out conservative batch-formation timeout and re-run harness.
4) If KV-related: disable new eviction policy, and run kvcache-specific microbench.
5) Communicate: create a short incident note in #eng-serving-runtime with summary, link to artifacts, recommended revert or mitigation.

Examples (command snippets):
- Run a single kernel A/B job on perf cluster:
  ./perf-harness --model llama-13b --hw a100-80 --quant fp16,int8 --trial ab-129 --concurrency 32 --seq-dist "short:0.8,long:0.2" --sample-traces 100

- Local smoke kv-warm test (docker):
  docker run --gpus all perf-harness:latest --recipe cold-kv-walk --runs 250 --seed 42

Observations from last 3 runs (journal):
- 2025-02-21: saw a 12% p95 increase on H100 for 13B when the new kernel fusion logic landed in PR 1287. Traces showed kernel_variant switch from fused-opt to fused-opt-v2, and kernel_ms increased on seq_len 512. Action: revert fused-opt-v2 rollout and pin kernel selection until perf validation. (See linked PR)
- 2025-02-25: kvcache eviction spikes in mixed workloads when concurrent weight-loading background job runs. Host CPU contention inside memmgr caused mutex contention; mitigated by moving background loader to lower niceness and reducing parallelism.
- 2025-02-28: batcher fairness regression introduced by a change to batch-timeout heuristics — long requests were being unfairly deprioritized causing p99 spikes. Short-term fix: restore previous timeout heuristic; long-term: add priority lanes for long-seq requests.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should the baseline store include a time-decayed baseline to account for gradual infra improvements? (pros/cons: avoids constant alerts but may hide slow degradations).
- Add per-batch kernel contention metric: how many kernels queued per GPU before dispatch? Need new probe.
- Formalize SLA-triggered canary: an automated canary that runs the two critical microbench recipes on any runtime PR that touches batcher/kernel selection.

Checklist before marking a regression ticket resolved:
- Reproduce regression locally and on perf cluster.
- Identify root cause and link code change(s).
- Confirm fix in bench harness with >= 3 independent runs.
- Update baseline if regression was due to intended change (with sign-off).
- Close ticket and annotate with artifact bundle hash.

Appendix: quick metric reference (field -> meaning)
- kernel_ms: measured GPU kernel runtime for the dispatch in question (ms)
- kvcache_warm_start: true/false (whether request started with prepopulated kv)
- gpu_queue_ms: wall time spent waiting on GPU queue before kernel launch
- batch_size_formed: actual batch size that was dispatched

Contacts: Evan Brooks (owner), Aisha Patel (kv-cache lead), Marco Liu (batcher lead)

Notes: This is an iterative working doc. Capture more regression cases as they occur and keep the baseline directory tidy. If you add new instrumentation fields, update the trace parser in perf-analysis/parse_traces.py and add corresponding columns to metrics.csv generation.
